title: Introduction
description: What spana is, why it exists, its dual-channel web-first engine, and its core principles.

sections.text: spana ( spana-test ) is a web-first, TypeScript-native end-to-end testing framework across Web, Android (Capacitor/WebView & React Native), iOS (WKWebView & React Native), Electron, and Electrobun — one { testID } selector model, zero Appium required locally.

sections.heading: Why spana
sections.text: Existing E2E tools force a painful split: - Web-only tools (Playwright, Cypress) are fast on desktop browsers but cannot drive native mobile WebViews, OS sheets ( SFSafariViewController , Chrome Custom Tabs, permission dialogs), or native mobile gestures. - Mobile-first runners (Appium/WebdriverIO, Maestro) add heavy middleware, JVM/YAML layers, or brittle full-tree XML dumps on every single tap. Spana bridges both worlds with a Dual-Channel Web-First Engine : 1. Fast DOM Lane: { testID } queries pierce Shadow DOM and same-origin s via the built-in Playwright DOM channel, the direct CDP engine ( execution.web.engine: "cdp" or "auto" ), spana-bridge , Android CDP, Lightpanda CDP, iOS WebKit Inspector, or Apple webinspectord , paired with MutationObserver reactive waits. 2. Native & System UI Lane: Real OS touches and out-of-process native sheets ( systemUI() ) go directly to persistent warm UiAutomator2 / WebDriverAgent daemons (with session reuse) — or to BrowserStack / Sauce Labs in Appium cloud mode.

sections.heading: Key principles
sections.text: - Pure TypeScript (plus optional Gherkin / BDD). Full autocomplete, imports, composable lazy fixtures ( createFlowWithFixtures ), and named setups ( defineSetup ). Works with both Bun and Node.js 20+. - Zero-setup fast path, opt-in superpowers. Works with zero app modification out of the box, and supports an opt-in spana-bridge WebSocket package for instant storage injection, fast reset, network mocking, and lazy idle detection across hybrid mobile and desktop shells. - Agent-native from day one. Ships a model-free stdio MCP server ( spana mcp ), a Verified Replay Cache for agentic steps ( .spana/cache/ ), pluggable CI Filters ( filters + --changed-since , including an optional LLM decision judge), and versioned --json envelopes on agent-facing commands. - Engineered for raw speed. Speculative CLI browser pre-launch, an opt-in direct CDP web engine (no Playwright pipe), persistent warm Chromium/WDA/UA2 daemons, multi-context browser worker pools, app.fill() one-call form fills, MutationObserver reactive waits + optional failFastWhenIdle , instantAnimations , blockResources , and auto-persisted longest-first --parallel scheduling.

title: Quick Start
description: Install spana, configure it, and run your first flow.

sections.heading: 1. Install
sections.text: npm install spana-test or bun add spana-test spana works with Node.js 20+ and Bun.

sections.heading: 2. Create a config file
sections.text: Create spana.config.ts at the root of your project: apps: { web: { url: "http://localhost:3000" }, android: { packageName: "com.example.app" }, ios: { bundleId: "com.example.app" }, }, platforms: ["web"], }); Start with platforms: ["web"] while getting familiar with the framework, then add "android" and "ios" once your device targets are set up.

sections.heading: 3. Write a flow
sections.text: Create flows/login.flow.ts : await app.tap({ testID: "email-input" }); await app.inputText("user@example.com"); await app.tap({ testID: "password-input" }); await app.inputText("secret"); await app.tap({ testID: "login-button" }); await expect({ testID: "home-screen" }).toBeVisible(); }); The testID selector maps to data-testid on web, accessibilityIdentifier on iOS, and resource-id on Android. It is the preferred selector type.

sections.heading: 4. Run
sections.text: spana test This discovers all .flow.ts , .test.ts , and .feature files under ./flows (or the flowDir in your config) and runs them against the configured platforms. Other .ts files in the folder are not picked up as flows.

sections.heading: Run a single file
sections.text: spana test flows/login.flow.ts

sections.heading: Target a specific platform
sections.text: spana test --platform android

sections.heading: Filter by tag
sections.text: spana test --tag smoke

sections.heading: 5. View results
sections.text: By default, results print to the console. To get structured JSON output: spana test --reporter json On failure, spana captures screenshots and diagnostics under spana-output/ by default (configurable via artifacts.outputDir ).

title: Run it the fastest way
description: The order to try Spana's run modes in, fastest first, and when to fall back to a slower one.

sections.text: Spana can run the same tests in several ways. Use the first option that fits your case. Fall back to the next one only when the "Does not apply when" column matches you.

sections.heading: Running a test suite
sections.text: Use this How Does not apply when --- -------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 spana test with .flow.ts or Gherkin .feature files npx spana test Your team needs Varar Markdown specs. They run in Vitest, so options 2–6 do not apply. 2 Only the flows a change can affect Local: spana test --changed or --last-failed . CI: --changed-since origin/main and a filters list No filters in spana.config.ts : then --changed-since runs every flow. A config or lockfile change runs every flow. 3 Web: shared browser pool spana test --platform web --workers 4 (or defaults.workers: 4 ). Flows reuse warm browser contexts. Flows must not share any browser state: use 3b. engine: "lightpanda" (one worker only). --parallel without --workers uses one worker. 3b Web, fully isolated flows execution.web.engine: "auto" (direct CDP for Chromium) plus execution.web.freshContextPerFlow: true (defaults to fast "hot-cache" isolation; set contextIsolation: "fresh" for brand-new browser contexts) You need wsEndpoint , a browser channel , HAR artifacts or a non-Chromium browser: "auto" then falls back to Playwright. 4 Hybrid, Electron or Electrobun: spana-bridge execution.bridge.enabled: true in config, and call initSpanaBridge() from spana-bridge in the app's test build You cannot change the app. Pure native React Native screens (no WebView DOM). Multi-worker web runs (use 3). 5 Skip UI sign-in Web: execution.web.storageState: "./auth/user.json" Not web. On mobile and desktop, use the bridge ( 4) to inject sign-in state. 6 Keep drivers warm between runs Web: execution.web.warmBrowser: true (Chromium only). Mobile: execution.warmDaemons.enabled: true Not Chromium. cdpUrl or wsEndpoint is set. 7 Local devices, cold start spana test --platform android,ios You need real devices you do not have locally. 8 Appium server or device cloud (slowest) --driver appium --appium-url , or BrowserStack / Sauce Labs — Measured on the 20-flow web benchmark: shared pool with 4 workers 3.04 s, bridge with 1 worker 3.92 s, direct CDP with a fresh context per flow and 4 workers 7.66 s, Playwright with 4 workers 10.74 s. See the comparison page for the method. Example CI command that combines 2 and 3: spana test --platform web --workers 4 --changed-since origin/main The CI/CD guide shows the filters config that --changed-since needs.

sections.heading: Tuning options
sections.text: These options make each flow faster. Each one is safe to turn on unless your tests check the thing it turns off. Option What it does Leave it off when ---------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------- execution.web.instantAnimations: true Sets CSS transitions and animations to almost zero time. You test animations. execution.web.blockResources: ["image", "font", "media"] Stops heavy downloads during web runs. You test images, fonts, media or visual snapshots. execution.web.waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" Continues as soon as the HTML is parsed, not after every asset loads (default "load" ). Your app needs all assets before it can respond. defaults.failFastWhenIdle: true Fails a web element wait early when the page is idle and loaded, instead of waiting the full timeout. Elements appear late without network or DOM activity. defaults.tapMode: "dom" Taps found in the DOM use a synthetic click instead of a real native touch. You need real touch events (gestures, native sheets). execution.web.contextIsolation "hot-cache" (default on Direct CDP) wipes cookies/storage/OPFS/IDB while keeping HTTP & V8 caches warm; "fresh" creates a brand-new context per flow. You need strict per-flow cache cold-starts ( "fresh" ). execution.web.maxContextsPerBrowser Contexts sharing one multiplexed browser process under parallel runs (default 4 with engine: "cdp" , else 2). — defaults.actionStableFrames Consecutive animation frames an element's rect must stay still before clicking (default 2 ; set 0 for static UIs). Elements slide/animate into place before clicks. Programmatic runTestCommand() import { runTestCommand } from "spana-test" runs flows in-process with zero CLI subprocess spawn overhead. You want isolated OS processes ( --processes ). In your app, set window. SPANA APP READY = false at start and true when the app is ready (a function that returns a boolean also works). When this value is defined, Spana waits for it before each DOM action, instead of acting on a loading screen. See Debugging.

sections.heading: Coding agents: exploring a screen and writing tests
sections.text: Use this Why Does not apply when --- ------------------------------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 1 spana mcp One live session for all tool calls. The agent does not start a new browser each time. Your agent has no MCP support. 2 spana selectors , spana hierarchy , spana validate Plain CLI. Works in any agent. You call them many times in a row: each call starts a new browser or driver session. 3 connect() from spana-test/agent Custom scripts, or other test runners such as Varar in Vitest. You want speed: no shared pool, no warm browser, no bridge. When the agent has a working flow, save it as a .flow.ts file and run it with spana test (suite option 1).

sections.heading: apps
sections.text: Defines the app targets for each platform. apps: { web?: { url?: string; bridge?: BridgeConfig }; android?: { packageName?: string; appPath?: string; cdpPort?: number; bridge?: BridgeConfig }; ios?: { bundleId?: string; appPath?: string; signing?: IOSSigningConfig; webkitInspectorUrl?: string; webkitInspectorPort?: number; bridge?: BridgeConfig; }; electron?: ElectronAppConfig; electrobun?: ElectrobunAppConfig; } Field Platform Description ------------------------- ----------- ------------------------------------------------------------- web.url Web Base URL the browser navigates to on launch android.packageName Android Android application ID (e.g. com.example.app ) ios.bundleId iOS iOS bundle identifier (e.g. com.example.app ) appPath Android/iOS Path to .app , .ipa , or .apk for auto-install signing.teamId iOS Apple Development Team ID (required for physical devices) signing.signingIdentity iOS Code signing identity (default: "Apple Development" ) cdpPort Android Explicit CDP port for Android WebView DOM access webkitInspectorUrl/Port iOS Explicit WebKit Inspector target for WKWebView DOM access bridge All Per-app spana-bridge override (replaces execution.bridge ) apps.electron launches an Electron app ( entry or executablePath , plus args , cwd , env , url ) or attaches to a running one with cdpUrl / cdpPort . apps.electrobun takes executablePath or appDir , args , cwd , env , renderer ( "native" or "cef" ), cdpUrl / cdpPort , webkitInspectorPort , and url . Both accept bridge .

sections.heading: platforms
sections.text: platforms?: Array Which platforms to run tests on by default. Can be overridden per-flow with FlowConfig.platforms and at the CLI with --platform . Default: ["web"]

sections.heading: parallelPlatforms
sections.text: parallelPlatforms?: boolean Run platform groups concurrently instead of serially. Default: false This is most useful when your web, Android, and iOS runs use independent resources. CLI parallel controls such as --parallel , --workers , and --devices can still force concurrent execution for the selected run.

sections.heading: flowDir
sections.text: flowDir?: string Directory to discover flow files from. spana searches it recursively for .flow.ts , .test.ts , and .feature files. A single file path also works. Default: "./flows" Relative paths are resolved from the directory that contains the config file, not from the current shell directory.

sections.heading: reporters
sections.text: reporters?: string[] One or more reporter names or custom reporter module paths. Available reporters: Name Output --------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------ console Human-readable terminal output (default) json Structured JSON events to stdout junit JUnit XML — compatible with CI artifact ingestion html Self-contained HTML report with embedded screenshots allure Allure-compatible result files github Markdown summary ( github-pr-summary.md ) and GitHub Actions job summary Default: ["console"] A custom reporter is a relative path (e.g. "./reporters/slack.ts" ) whose default export is a Reporter object or a (options: { outputDir: string }) = Reporter factory. See Custom Reporters.

sections.heading: execution
sections.text: Execution mode and remote Appium settings. execution?: { mode?: "local" "appium"; web?: { browser?: "chromium" "firefox" "webkit"; engine?: "playwright" "auto" "cdp" "lightpanda"; cdpUrl?: string; wsEndpoint?: string; executablePath?: string; channel?: string; headless?: boolean; waitUntil?: "domcontentloaded" "load" "networkidle" "commit"; instantAnimations?: boolean; blockResources?: Array ; warmBrowser?: boolean; warmBrowserScope?: string; freshContextPerFlow?: boolean; contextIsolation?: "hot-cache" "fresh"; maxContextsPerBrowser?: number; virtualAuthenticator?: boolean VirtualAuthenticatorOptions; storageState?: string; verboseLogging?: boolean; storybook?: { url?: string; iframePath?: string; }; }; bridge?: { enabled?: boolean; port?: number; // default 9333 host?: string; // default "127.0.0.1" url?: string; connectTimeout?: number; // ms, default 5000 }; warmDaemons?: { enabled?: boolean; reuseSession?: boolean; stateFile?: string; }; appium?: { serverUrl?: string; capabilities?: Record ; platformCapabilities?: { android?: Record ; ios?: Record ; }; capabilitiesFile?: string; autoStart?: boolean; autoStartBinary?: string; autoStartArgs?: string[]; reportToProvider?: boolean; cloudProvider?: string; browserstack?: { app?: { id?: string; path?: string; name?: string; customId?: string }; local?: { enabled?: boolean; binary?: string; identifier?: string; args?: string[] }; options?: Record ; }; saucelabs?: { app?: { id?: string; path?: string; name?: string }; connect?: { enabled?: boolean; binary?: string; tunnelName?: string; args?: string[] }; options?: Record ; }; }; } Use execution.web to configure the local browser runtime for web flows. Field Description ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- browser Browser for local web runs: chromium (default), firefox , or webkit engine "playwright" (default), "cdp" (direct CDP to Chromium, no Playwright pipe), "lightpanda" (connects to cdpUrl , default http://127.0.0.1:9222 ), or "auto" (see below) cdpUrl Connect to an existing CDP browser or Lightpanda endpoint instead of launching one wsEndpoint Connect to a remote Playwright server (e.g. BrowserStack Automate) executablePath Explicit browser binary channel Playwright browser channel such as "chrome" or "msedge" headless Run without a visible browser window (default true ) waitUntil Navigation readiness event for launch / openLink (default "load" ) instantAnimations Collapse CSS transitions and animations for faster, deterministic runs blockResources Abort image , font , media , or stylesheet requests warmBrowser Reuse a persistent warm Chromium process across runs (Chromium only; falls back to warmDaemons.enabled ) warmBrowserScope Key that isolates warm browsers between concurrent repos or runs freshContextPerFlow Isolate browser state between flows; defaults to "hot-cache" on Direct CDP (wipes cookies/storage/OPFS/IDB while keeping HTTP/V8 caches warm) contextIsolation Direct CDP isolation strategy when freshContextPerFlow is enabled: "hot-cache" (default, 4 ms reset) or "fresh" (brand-new Target.createBrowserContext per flow) maxContextsPerBrowser Max worker contexts sharing one browser process under --parallel (default 4 for cdp with multiplexed WebSocket, 2 otherwise) virtualAuthenticator Attach a WebAuthn virtual authenticator (passkeys) to each new context; true or an options object storageState Preload Playwright cookies and storage state from a JSON file verboseLogging Print verbose Playwright browser/page diagnostics to stdout storybook.url Dedicated Storybook origin for app.openStory() / Session.openStory() storybook.iframePath Override Storybook's preview iframe path, default /iframe.html engine: "auto" uses the direct CDP engine when browser is chromium and you have not set wsEndpoint , channel , or artifacts.har ; otherwise it uses Playwright. The direct CDP engine does not support app.getHAR() . storageState is resolved relative to spana.config.ts . Storybook uses URLs instead of filesystem paths, so it stays portable by pointing at the right origin for each environment. execution.bridge configures the optional in-app spana-bridge WebSocket server shared by WebView targets. It is enabled when enabled: true , or when you set port or url . execution.warmDaemons.enabled keeps WDA / UiAutomator2 daemons alive between runs (default false ); reuseSession (default true when enabled) reuses the active session; stateFile overrides where daemon metadata is stored. Use spana daemon status / spana daemon stop to inspect or stop them. Use mode: "appium" when running against BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, or another Appium-compatible grid. Field Description ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- serverUrl Remote Appium server URL capabilities / capabilitiesFile Raw desired capabilities, with file paths resolved relative to the config file platformCapabilities Extra capabilities merged on top of capabilities for android or ios autoStart Spawn a local appium process for the run (default false ; ignores serverUrl ) autoStartBinary / autoStartArgs Override the appium binary name and pass extra CLI args to it reportToProvider Mark the remote session passed/failed when the provider supports it cloudProvider Path to a custom cloud provider module that default-exports a CloudProvider browserstack BrowserStack upload, local tunnel, and capability helper settings saucelabs Sauce Labs upload, Sauce Connect, and capability helper settings Raw capabilities from execution.appium.capabilities , capabilitiesFile , and --caps-json remain the strongest override surface. Provider helper sections fill in missing provider-specific fields and can manage BrowserStack Local / Sauce Connect lifecycle when enabled. For a custom provider implementation, see Cloud Providers.

sections.heading: CLI precedence
sections.text: For spana test , CLI flags win over config values. CLI flag Config field ---------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------- --platform platforms --reporter reporters --retries defaults.retries --workers defaults.workers --driver execution.mode --appium-url execution.appium.serverUrl --appium-auto-start execution.appium.autoStart --caps / --caps-json execution.appium.capabilitiesFile / capabilities --changed-since Runs the configured filters --tag / --grep CLI-only flow selection --validate-config Validates config and exits --device / --devices CLI-only device selection --parallel Enables concurrent execution --watch / --changed / --last-failed CLI-only iteration controls --update-baselines CLI-only screenshot and ARIA baseline control --js-coverage artifacts.jsCoverage --shard / --bail CLI-only execution controls --debug-on-failure / --verbose / --quiet CLI-only output and debugging controls Sharding happens after tag/name/platform filtering so each shard gets a deterministic slice of the already-selected flows.

sections.heading: defaults
sections.text: Timing and retry defaults applied to all auto-wait operations. Individual operations can override these with WaitOptions . defaults?: { waitTimeout?: number; // ms pollInterval?: number; // ms settleTimeout?: number; // ms retries?: number; waitForIdleTimeout?: number; typingDelay?: number; initialPollInterval?: number; hierarchyCacheTtl?: number; retryDelay?: number; workers?: number; snapshotMaxDepth?: number; tapMode?: "native" "dom"; failFastWhenIdle?: boolean; } Option Default Description --------------------- ---------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ waitTimeout 5000 Maximum ms to wait for an assertion or element lookup pollInterval 200 Maximum ms between assertion polls settleTimeout 0 Stable time required before an assertion passes retries 0 Retry count for failed flow executions waitForIdleTimeout 0 Pause after mutating actions such as tap or scroll typingDelay 0 Delay between typed characters initialPollInterval 50 First poll interval before adaptive backoff ramps up hierarchyCacheTtl 100 Hierarchy cache freshness window in ms; set 0 to disable retryDelay 0 Delay between failed flow retry attempts workers — Default max workers per platform when --parallel is enabled snapshotMaxDepth 100 Max depth of iOS UI hierarchy snapshots tapMode "native" When a DOM channel finds the element: "native" real touch, or "dom" fast synthetic click failFastWhenIdle false On web, fail element waits early when the page is idle and fully loaded, instead of waiting the full waitTimeout

sections.heading: artifacts
sections.text: Controls screenshot and hierarchy capture on test completion. artifacts?: { outputDir?: string; captureOnFailure?: boolean; captureOnSuccess?: boolean; captureSteps?: boolean; screenshot?: boolean; uiHierarchy?: boolean; consoleLogs?: boolean; jsErrors?: boolean; har?: boolean; jsCoverage?: boolean; video?: "off" "on" "retain-on-failure"; playback?: boolean; } Option Default Description ------------------ ------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- outputDir "./spana-output" Directory to write captured artifacts captureOnFailure true Capture artifacts for failed flows captureOnSuccess false Capture final artifacts for passed flows captureSteps false Capture screenshots after each recorded step screenshot true Include screenshots in captures uiHierarchy true Include UI hierarchy dumps consoleLogs true Include captured browser console logs on web jsErrors true Include uncaught browser JavaScript errors on web har true Include HAR network traces on web jsCoverage false Write js-coverage.json as a flow attachment for Chromium web tests (Playwright or direct CDP) video "off" Record a video of each flow: "on" , or "retain-on-failure" to keep it only for failed flows playback false Keep a step-by-step visual playback timeline for the HTML report JavaScript coverage is collected for the primary page from before app launch through the end of the flow, whether the flow passes or fails. Secondary tabs and contexts are not included. Each flow gets a raw V8 coverage file; Spana does not merge coverage or generate a source-mapped report. Use spana test --js-coverage for a single run, or set artifacts: { jsCoverage: true } in the project or flow configuration.

sections.heading: hooks
sections.text: Lifecycle hooks that run around flow execution. Each hook receives a HookContext . hooks?: { beforeAll?: (ctx: HookContext) = Promise ; beforeEach?: (ctx: HookContext) = Promise ; afterEach?: (ctx: HookContext) = Promise ; afterAll?: (ctx: HookContext) = Promise ; } Hook When it runs ------------ --------------------------------------------------------- beforeAll Once before all flows on a platform beforeEach Before each individual flow afterEach After each individual flow (always runs, even on failure) afterAll Once after all flows on a platform beforeEach and afterEach receive app and platform , plus result in afterEach . beforeAll and afterAll run outside any flow, so they receive platform (and summary in afterAll ) but no app . beforeEach runs before the flow's automatic launch.

sections.heading: Error handling
sections.text: Hook On failure ------------ ----------------------------------------------------------- beforeAll All flows on that platform are skipped and marked as failed beforeEach That flow is skipped and marked as failed afterEach Warning logged, test result is not affected afterAll Warning logged, test results are not affected

sections.heading: Example
sections.text: hooks: { beforeEach: async ({ app }) = { await app.launch({ clearState: true }); }, afterEach: async ({ app, result }) = { if (result?.status === "failed") { console.log( Flow failed: ${result.name} ); } }, }, });

sections.heading: Per-flow configuration
sections.text: The flow() function accepts an optional config object as its second argument, letting you override global settings for a single flow. flow( "checkout", { timeout: 30000, tags: ["smoke"], artifacts: { captureSteps: true }, launchOptions: { deepLink: "myapp://checkout" }, }, async ({ app }) = { // ... }, ); interface FlowConfig { tags?: string[]; platforms?: Platform[]; timeout?: number; autoLaunch?: boolean; launchOptions?: LaunchOptions; artifacts?: ArtifactConfig; defaults?: FlowDefaults; when?: WhenCondition; } Option Default Description --------------- --------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------- tags [] Tags for CLI filtering with --tag platforms — Restrict a flow to specific platforms timeout defaults.waitTimeout × 10 , or 60000 Overall flow timeout in ms autoLaunch true Automatically launch the app before the flow starts launchOptions — Per-flow launch defaults merged on top of project launchOptions artifacts — Per-flow artifact overrides defaults — Per-flow wait, typing, cache, and idle timing overrides when — Runtime conditions such as platform or environment-variable gates The per-flow artifacts object is merged with the global artifacts config, so you only need to specify the fields you want to override. For example, enabling captureSteps on a single flow: flow( "visual regression", { artifacts: { captureSteps: true, captureOnSuccess: true } }, async ({ app }) = { // Every step is captured, and the final state is saved even on success }, );

sections.heading: launchOptions
sections.text: Default launch options applied to each flow launch. FlowConfig.launchOptions overrides these defaults for one flow, and explicit app.launch(opts) calls are merged on top of both. launchOptions?: LaunchOptions launchOptions: { clearState: true, // fresh state every run }, });

sections.heading: LaunchOptions reference
sections.text: interface LaunchOptions { clearState?: boolean; clearKeychain?: boolean; deepLink?: string; launchArguments?: Record ; deviceState?: DeviceStateConfig; } interface DeviceStateConfig { language?: string; locale?: string; timeZone?: string; } Option Default Description ----------------- ------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ clearState false Clear app data/storage before launch clearKeychain false Clear the iOS keychain before launch (simulator only) deepLink — Open the app via a deep link URL launchArguments — Key-value pairs passed as launch arguments to the app deviceState — Launch-time language / locale / time-zone overrides where the runtime can honor them Platform behavior Option Web Android iOS ----------------- ---------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- clearState Clears cookies, localStorage adb shell pm clear Resets app permissions clearKeychain No-op No-op (warns) xcrun simctl keychain reset launchArguments No-op Passed as --es extras via am start Appium iOS: process args via mobile: launchApp ; local WDA: warns + ignores deviceState Warns + ignores Appium: session-start caps; local Android: warns + ignores Appium: session caps + launch-time process config; local WDA: warns + ignores deepLink Navigates to URL adb shell am start -d xcrun simctl openurl / WDA Android launchArguments are string extras. For example: await app.launch({ launchArguments: { featureFlag: "on", buildVariant: "staging", }, }); deviceState is for launch-time localization and time-zone setup. It does not mutate the device clock mid-run. In Appium mode, suite-level launchOptions.deviceState is also mapped into session capabilities so defaults apply even when Appium keeps autoLaunch off. Common locale forms such as fr CA / fr-CA are normalized for Appium, but Android still needs both language and region information available. Per-flow usage Use FlowConfig.launchOptions when one flow needs a different launch profile than the project defaults: flow( "checkout in French", { autoLaunch: true, launchOptions: { clearState: true, deepLink: "myapp://checkout", deviceState: { language: "fr", locale: "fr CA", timeZone: "America/Toronto", }, }, }, async ({ app }) = { // ... }, ); When autoLaunch is false , you can still call app.launch() manually. The project and per-flow defaults are merged first, then the manual call wins: flow("onboarding", { autoLaunch: false }, async ({ app }) = { await app.launch({ deepLink: "myapp://welcome" }); // ... });

title: Spana vs Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO, Maestro, Detox, Appium, Argent & e2e
description: An honest, feature-by-feature comparison of Spana with Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO, Maestro, Detox, Appium, Argent, and e2e — platforms, capabilities, speed scores, and live benchmark numbers.

sections.text: Spana is a TypeScript E2E framework where one test runs on Web, iOS, Android, Electron, and Electrobun. No single framework wins every row — this page grades 9 E2E frameworks honestly on platforms, authoring, CI scale, debugging, AI workflows, ecosystem maturity, and speed so you can pick the right tool for your stack (even when that tool isn't Spana). :::note[Direct CDP + Playwright compatibility] On Chromium, Spana's engine: "auto" / "cdp" talks directly to Chromium over a raw CDP WebSocket (bypassing Playwright's Node client↔server pipe, including cross-origin OOPIF iframes, live screencast video playback, and pre-warmed isolated BrowserContext pools). When you choose Firefox, WebKit, or Playwright-specific options like HAR recording, Spana seamlessly uses its bundled Playwright driver with the exact same flow API. :::

sections.heading: Benchmarks
sections.text: Web runs: Apple M4 Pro, Bun 1.4.5, headless Chrome. 20 flows with 14 steps each (280 steps in total). Playwright and Spana sign in once through the UI, then reuse the session for the other flows. How the other tools are run: - Playwright rows use the Playwright library directly (one browser, a new context per flow). They do not use the playwright test runner. - WebDriver HTTP is a simulation of the W3C WebDriver protocol that WebdriverIO uses: plain HTTP calls to a small local WebDriver server. It does not use the webdriverio package, so treat it as a rough guide to protocol cost, not a WebdriverIO result.

sections.heading: When to pick something else
sections.text: - Playwright — your app is web-only and you want the largest community, the best time-travel Trace Viewer ( trace.zip ), first-class VS Code debugging, or Python / Java / .NET SDKs. - Cypress — you want mature built-in Component Testing (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte) and an interactive in-browser time-travel runner for frontend teams. - WebdriverIO — you want a battle-tested OpenJS ecosystem with real Safari, official Electron & component runners, or an existing WebDriver / Appium grid. - Maestro — you want ultra-simple YAML mobile tests that non-developers and QA teams can read and write with minimal boilerplate. - Detox — you test only a React Native app and want gray-box synchronization directly with the app's JavaScript thread and timers. - Appium — you need native desktop/TV drivers Spana does not have (macOS, Windows, tvOS, Roku), every real-device cloud out of the box, or Java / Python / C / Ruby tests. - Argent — you're a React Native / TV / macOS team that wants deep Hermes, React DevTools, Xcode Instruments, and Perfetto profiling driven directly by AI coding agents. - e2e — you want natural-language agent.act() / agent.assert() steps mixed directly into TypeScript tests with built-in CLI replay caching.

sections.heading: When Spana fits best
sections.text: - One app across Web, iOS, Android, Electron, and/or Electrobun maintained in a single typed TypeScript (or Gherkin) suite. - A Capacitor, Ionic, React Native, or Electron app with testID attributes where dual-channel DOM + native access avoids Appium setup. - You want Chromium Direct CDP speed (1.5–1.7× strict, up to 3.8× hot-cache ), Rust visual diffing, and PR diff filtering with zero paid CI gates. - You want a model-free MCP server ( spana mcp ) so coding agents can inspect screens, drive live sessions across all 5 targets, and export deterministic .flow.ts tests. title: Flows
description: The flow() API — defining, configuring, and exporting test flows.

sections.text: A flow is the basic unit of a spana test. Each flow file exports a single FlowDefinition as its default export. spana discovers flow files named .flow.ts or .test.ts (plus .feature for Gherkin).

sections.heading: Defining a flow
sections.text: flow() has two overloads: // Without config flow(name: string, fn: FlowFn): FlowDefinition // With config flow(name: string, config: FlowConfig, fn: FlowFn): FlowDefinition

sections.heading: Basic flow
sections.text: await app.tap({ testID: "email-input" }); await app.inputText("user@example.com"); await app.tap({ testID: "login-button" }); await expect({ testID: "home-screen" }).toBeVisible(); });

sections.text: "checkout flow", { tags: ["smoke", "payments"], platforms: ["android", "ios"], timeout: 60000, autoLaunch: true, launchOptions: { deepLink: "myapp://checkout", }, }, async ({ app, expect, platform }) = { // ... }, );

sections.heading: FlowContext
sections.text: The function receives a FlowContext object: interface FlowContext { app: PromiseApp; expect: (selector: ExtendedSelector) = PromiseExpectation; platform: Platform; sessions: Sessions; } Property Type Description ---------- ---------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- app PromiseApp App interaction API — tap, type, scroll, launch, etc. expect (selector) = PromiseExpectation Assertion API — toBeVisible , toBeHidden , toHaveText platform Platform "web" , "android" , "ios" , "electron" , or "electrobun" sessions Sessions sessions.open({ name, platform: "web", ... }) opens an extra named web session in the same flow

sections.heading: FlowConfig
sections.text: interface FlowConfig { tags?: string[]; platforms?: Platform[]; timeout?: number; autoLaunch?: boolean; launchOptions?: LaunchOptions; artifacts?: ArtifactConfig; defaults?: FlowDefaults; when?: WhenCondition; skip?: boolean (WhenCondition & { reason?: string }); fixme?: boolean (WhenCondition & { reason?: string }); only?: boolean; retries?: number; } interface WhenCondition { platform?: Platform Platform[]; env?: string; } Option Type Default Description ---------------- -------------------- --------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- tags string[] — Tag strings for --tag filtering at the CLI platforms Platform[] all configured Restrict this flow to specific platforms only timeout number defaults.waitTimeout × 10 , or 60000 Flow-level timeout in milliseconds autoLaunch boolean true Automatically launch the app before the flow starts launchOptions LaunchOptions config default Override launch defaults for this flow and for manual app.launch artifacts ArtifactConfig config default Override capture behavior for this single flow defaults FlowDefaults config default Override wait / typing / stability defaults per flow when WhenCondition — Runtime conditions that control whether the flow runs skip / fixme Boolean or condition false Do not execute the flow; fixme identifies a known issue in reports only boolean false If any selected flow is focused, only focused flows run retries number Project or CLI retry count Number of additional attempts after a failure; 0 disables retries

sections.heading: Skip, focus, or retry individual flows
sections.text: "Updates device settings", { fixme: { platform: "ios", reason: "Waiting for a simulator fix" }, retries: 1 }, async ({ app }) = { await app.tap({ testID: "settings" }); }, ); skip and fixme conditions are evaluated per target platform. If both platform and env are given, both must match (the environment variable must be nonempty). Reports count both as skipped and retain the modifier and optional reason. Use flow.skip(name, fn) , flow.fixme(name, fn) , or flow.only(name, fn) as shorthand; each also accepts a config argument. Remove only before committing so the rest of the suite runs in CI.

sections.heading: Per-flow launch overrides
sections.text: FlowConfig.launchOptions is merged on top of the project launchOptions , and explicit app.launch(opts) calls are merged last. "launch in French", { autoLaunch: true, launchOptions: { deepLink: "myapp://checkout", deviceState: { language: "fr", locale: "fr CA", }, }, }, async ({ expect }) = { await expect({ testID: "checkout-screen" }).toBeVisible(); }, );

sections.heading: Conditional execution with when
sections.text: The when field lets you skip flows based on runtime conditions. Platform condition when.platform is checked once, against the whole set of platforms selected for the run. The flow is dropped only when none of the selected platforms match. Unlike platforms , it does not skip the flow on each non-matching platform inside a multi-platform run. Use platforms when a flow must never run on a given platform. // skipped when the run does not include iOS }); You can also pass an array: "mobile-only test", { when: { platform: ["ios", "android"] } }, async ({ app, expect }) = { // skipped when the run targets only web }, ); Environment variable condition when.env skips the flow unless the specified environment variable is set to a non-empty value: "CI smoke test", { when: { env: "CI" }, tags: ["smoke"], }, async ({ app, expect }) = { // only runs when CI is set to any non-empty value }, );

sections.heading: The app API
sections.text: All methods return Promise unless noted.

sections.heading: Core interaction
sections.text: Method Signature Description -------------------- ------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- tap (selector, opts?) = Promise Tap an element tapXY (x, y) = Promise Tap at absolute coordinates doubleTap (selector, opts?) = Promise Double-tap an element longPress (selector, opts?) = Promise Long-press an element longPressXY (x, y, opts?) = Promise Long-press at coordinates inputText (text) = Promise Type text into the focused element fill (selector, value, opts?) = Promise Wait for a field, focus it, replace its value, and fire input/change events pressKey (key) = Promise Press a named key hideKeyboard () = Promise Dismiss the software keyboard dismissKeyboard (opts?) = Promise Use a platform-aware keyboard dismissal strategy swipe (direction, opts?) = Promise Swipe in a direction scroll (direction) = Promise Scroll in a direction scrollUntilVisible (selector, opts?) = Promise Scroll until a target becomes visible backUntilVisible (selector, opts?) = Promise Use system back until a target becomes visible Direction values are "up" "down" "left" "right" . When a DOM channel is connected (web, and WebViews reached via CDP or spana-bridge ), fill() does all of this in one in-page call. On native-only elements it falls back to a tap plus inputText() , which does not clear the existing value. dismissKeyboard() defaults to an auto strategy that uses the driver-specific keyboard dismissal path and falls back to Android system back when needed. scrollUntilVisible() and backUntilVisible() are useful for replacing ad hoc retry loops in mobile-heavy flows.

sections.heading: Advanced gestures
sections.text: Method Signature Description ------------ ----------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------- pinch (selector, { scale?, duration? }?) = Promise Perform a pinch gesture on an element zoom (selector, { scale?, duration? }?) = Promise Perform a zoom gesture on an element multiTouch (sequences) = Promise Run multiple touch sequences together These gestures are only available on mobile runtimes. Use them for map canvases, image viewers, and multi-finger interactions that are awkward to model with repeated taps.

sections.heading: App lifecycle and navigation
sections.text: Method Signature Description ------------ -------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------- launch (opts?) = Promise Launch the app, optionally with a deep link stop () = Promise Stop the app kill () = Promise Force-kill the app clearState () = Promise Clear app data/state openLink (url) = Promise Open a URL or deep link openStory (storyId, options?) = Promise Open a Storybook story inside the web runtime back () = Promise Press the Android back button or browser history back openStory() is web-only. It uses execution.web.storybook when configured and falls back to apps.web.url plus Storybook's iframe.html .

sections.heading: Element queries and utilities
sections.text: Method Signature Description ---------------- --------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------- takeScreenshot (name?) = Promise Capture a screenshot and return the bytes getText (selector, opts?) = Promise Read the current element text getAttribute (selector, name, opts?) = Promise Read an element attribute isVisible (selector, { timeout? }?) = Promise Check visibility without failing the flow (default timeout 1000 ms) isEnabled (selector, opts?) = Promise Check whether an element is enabled evaluate (fn \ string, ...args) = Promise Run JavaScript in the page or WebView context getText() , getAttribute() , isVisible() , and isEnabled() are useful when you need branching logic instead of a hard assertion.

sections.heading: Browser runtime helpers
sections.text: Method Signature Description ---------------------------- -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- mockNetwork (matcher, response) = Promise Fulfill matching requests with a mocked response blockNetwork (matcher) = Promise Abort matching requests clearNetworkMocks () = Promise Remove active route mocks or blocks setNetworkConditions (conditions) = Promise Simulate network conditions — profiles, custom throttling, or offline mode saveCookies (path) = Promise Save Playwright cookies to a JSON file loadCookies (path) = Promise Load cookies from a JSON file saveAuthState (path) = Promise Save Playwright storage state to disk loadAuthState (path) = Promise Replace the browser context with saved auth state downloadFile (path) = Promise Save the next browser download to disk uploadFile (selector, path) = Promise Upload a local file through a file input newTab (url?) = Promise Open a new browser tab and return its ID switchToTab (index) = Promise Switch to a tab by index closeTab () = Promise Close the current tab getTabIds () = Promise List known browser tab IDs getConsoleLogs () = Promise Read captured browser console messages getJSErrors () = Promise Read captured uncaught JavaScript errors getHAR () = Promise Read the recorded HTTP Archive for the current run (Playwright engine only) getPage () = T Escape hatch: the underlying Playwright Page or CDP page object (synchronous) enableVirtualAuthenticator (opts?) = Promise Add a WebAuthn virtual authenticator (passkeys) and return its ID removeVirtualAuthenticator (id?) = Promise Remove a virtual authenticator (default: the latest one) getVirtualCredentials (id?) = Promise List credentials stored in the virtual authenticator clearVirtualCredentials (id?) = Promise Delete credentials stored in the virtual authenticator These helpers are available on local web runs with the Playwright or direct CDP engine. getHAR() needs the Playwright engine. mockNetwork , blockNetwork , getConsoleLogs , and getJSErrors are also implemented for Electron, Electrobun, and mobile WebViews. On Android, use a debuggable WebView or spana-bridge ; on iOS, use spana-bridge . Bridge mocks intercept JavaScript fetch/XHR only. Neither option intercepts native HTTP clients. When artifact capture is enabled, failures can also write console logs, JavaScript errors, and HAR files into spana-output/ . setNetworkConditions() Simulate degraded or offline network conditions across all platforms. You can use a named profile or supply custom values. Available profiles: wifi , 4g , 3g , 2g , edge , offline // Simulate 3G network await app.setNetworkConditions({ profile: "3g" }); // Go offline await app.setNetworkConditions({ profile: "offline" }); // Back to normal await app.setNetworkConditions({ profile: "wifi" }); Custom values still work when you need fine-grained control: await app.setNetworkConditions({ latencyMs: 150, downloadThroughputKbps: 1000, uploadThroughputKbps: 500, }); Platform support: Platform Offline Profiles Custom Values -------------------- ------- ---------- ------------- Web (Chromium) Yes Yes Yes Web (Firefox/WebKit) Yes No No Android emulator Yes Yes Yes Android device Yes No No iOS simulator Yes Yes (sudo) Yes (sudo) Appium cloud Yes Yes varies flow("web app can run with mocked APIs", async ({ app, platform }) = { if (platform !== "web") return; await app.loadAuthState("./auth/user.json"); await app.mockNetwork(" /api/profile", { json: { id: "demo", name: "Demo User" }, }); await app.blockNetwork(" /analytics/ "); await app.setNetworkConditions({ profile: "3g" }); await app.evaluate(() = console.info("profile hydrated")); const logs = await app.getConsoleLogs(); const jsErrors = await app.getJSErrors(); const har = await app.getHAR(); if (!logs.some((entry) = entry.text.includes("profile hydrated"))) { throw new Error("Expected the profile hydration log to be captured."); } if (jsErrors.length 0) { throw new Error( Unexpected JS errors: ${jsErrors.map((entry) = entry.message).join(", ")} ); } if (!Array.isArray((har as { log?: { entries?: unknown[] } }).log?.entries)) { throw new Error("Expected HAR output to contain request entries."); } await app.saveCookies("./tmp/cookies.json"); });

sections.heading: Storybook-backed component flows
sections.text: Storybook is a good isolated surface for Spana's web runtime when you want component-level checks without giving up real-browser automation. flow("primary button story passes smoke checks", async ({ app, expect, platform }) = { if (platform !== "web") return; await app.openStory("components-button--primary", { args: { label: "Save", disabled: false }, globals: { theme: "dark" }, }); await expect({ text: "Save" }).toBeVisible(); await expect({ text: "Save" }).toMatchScreenshot("storybook-button"); }); Set execution.web.storybook.url when Storybook runs on a different origin from your main app. args and globals support scalar values ( string , number , boolean , null ).

sections.heading: Fast state helpers
sections.text: Method Signature Description -------------- ---------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ waitForIdle (opts?) = Promise Wait for in-flight requests, animations, and renders to settle (needs spana-bridge ; no-op otherwise) setStorage (entries) = Promise Inject localStorage , sessionStorage , and cookies directly clearStorage (opts?) = Promise Clear localStorage and sessionStorage without a UI flow resetFast () = Promise Clear storage and reload instead of a full app reset, where the driver supports it; otherwise falls back to clearState setStorage and clearStorage run through evaluate() , so they work wherever evaluate() works. With spana-bridge connected, clearStorage can also clear cookies, IndexedDB, and Capacitor Preferences.

sections.heading: Hybrid / WebView helpers
sections.text: Method Signature Description ------------------- ------------------------------ ------------------------------------------ getContexts () = Promise List available native and WebView contexts getCurrentContext () = Promise Read the currently active context switchToContext (contextId) = Promise Switch to a specific context ID switchToWebView () = Promise Switch to the first available WebView switchToNativeApp () = Promise Switch back to the native app context These helpers are useful for hybrid apps where you need to move between native chrome and embedded web content.

sections.heading: JavaScript execution
sections.text: app.evaluate() runs JavaScript inside the browser page context. Use it to read DOM state, manipulate local storage, or access browser-only globals. flow("read page state", async ({ app, platform }) = { if (platform !== "web") return; const title = await app.evaluate(() = document.title); const count = await app.evaluate( (selector: string) = document.querySelectorAll(selector).length, "button", ); await app.evaluate(() = { localStorage.setItem("feature-flag", "true"); }); if (!title count === 0) { throw new Error("Expected page state to be readable from evaluate()."); } }); evaluate() runs in the web page on web, in the renderer on Electron / Electrobun, and in the WebView on mobile when a DOM channel (CDP, WebKit Inspector, or spana-bridge ) is reachable. Pure native screens have no JavaScript context.

sections.heading: Per-flow artifact overrides
sections.text: Use artifacts in FlowConfig when one flow needs different capture behavior from the global defaults. "checkout keeps extra diagnostics on success", { artifacts: { captureSteps: true, captureOnSuccess: true, consoleLogs: true, jsErrors: true, har: true, }, }, async ({ app, expect, platform }) = { if (platform === "web") { await app.openLink("/checkout"); } await expect({ text: "Checkout" }).toBeVisible(); }, ); Use the global config in Configuration for your default policy, then tighten or loosen capture per flow only where it helps debugging.

sections.heading: Settings export
sections.text: You can export named settings from a flow file to apply shared config to all flows in that file: tags: ["smoke"], timeout: 30000, }; // ... }); settings is shallow-merged on top of the flow's own FlowConfig , so a key set in both places takes the settings value.

title: Selectors
description: All selector types, how to use them, and how they map across platforms.

sections.text: A selector tells spana which element to interact with or assert on. Selectors are used by all app interaction methods and expect() .

sections.heading: testID (recommended)
sections.text: { testID: "login-button"; } The preferred selector. Maps to the platform's primary element identifier: Platform Attribute -------- ------------------------------------- Web data-testid (or testID ) attribute Android resource-id (last segment matched) iOS accessibilityIdentifier Add testID props to your React Native components: Sign In On web, this renders as data-testid="login-button" .

sections.heading: text
sections.text: { text: "Sign In"; } Matches against the visible label text of an element. Matching is a case-insensitive substring match — the element text only needs to contain the provided string. Use this when a testID is not available, such as for dynamic or third-party content.

sections.heading: accessibilityLabel
sections.text: { accessibilityLabel: "Close dialog"; } Matches the OS-level accessibility label exactly (on web, the aria-label attribute). Useful for elements that have a label distinct from their visible text (e.g. icon buttons).

sections.heading: System UI
sections.text: await app.tap(systemUI({ text: "Allow" })); // equivalent to: await app.tap({ text: "Allow", systemUI: true }); Add systemUI: true to a text or accessibilityLabel selector when it targets out-of-process OS UI, such as permission dialogs, SFSafariViewController , ASWebAuthenticationSession , or Chrome Custom Tabs. spana then skips the DOM channel and uses the native driver.

sections.heading: point
sections.text: { point: { x: 150, y: 340 } } Taps at absolute screen coordinates. Use as a last resort — coordinates are device-specific and break across screen sizes.

sections.heading: String shorthand
sections.text: A plain string is treated as a text selector (case-insensitive substring match), not as a testID : await app.tap("Sign In"); // matches the same elements as: await app.tap({ text: "Sign In" }); Use { testID: "..." } explicitly when you mean a test ID.

sections.heading: Relative selectors
sections.text: When multiple elements match the same selector, use relative positioning to disambiguate. A relative selector wraps a base selector with directional constraints: // Tap the "Edit" button below the "Email" label await app.tap({ selector: { text: "Edit" }, below: { text: "Email" } }); // Tap the button to the right of the "Username" label await app.tap({ selector: { testID: "action-btn" }, rightOf: { text: "Username" } }); // Find an element inside a specific container await app.tap({ selector: { text: "Submit" }, childOf: { testID: "login-form" } }); Constraint Description ---------- --------------------------------------------------- below Element must be below the anchor (closest first) above Element must be above the anchor (closest first) leftOf Element must be left of the anchor (closest first) rightOf Element must be right of the anchor (closest first) childOf Element must be a descendant of the anchor Constraints can be combined — all must match: // Button below the header AND to the right of the label await app.tap({ selector: { testID: "btn" }, below: { text: "Header" }, rightOf: { text: "Label" }, }); Relative selectors work with the selector-based interaction methods ( tap , doubleTap , longPress , etc.) and assertions ( expect().toBeVisible() , etc.).

sections.heading: Selector priority
sections.text: When spana builds a suggested selector (e.g. in spana selectors output), it uses this priority: 1. testID — most stable, preferred 2. accessibilityLabel 3. text

sections.heading: WaitOptions
sections.text: All selector-based methods accept an optional WaitOptions object to override the global defaults for that specific call: await app.tap({ testID: "slow-element" }, { timeout: 10000 }); await expect({ testID: "result" }).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000, pollInterval: 500 }); Option Type Description --------------------- ------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- timeout number ms to wait before failing pollInterval number ms between hierarchy polls settleTimeout number ms the element must be stable before matching initialPollInterval number first poll interval before adaptive backoff tapMode "native" \ "dom" for taps resolved via a DOM channel: real touch or synthetic click failFastWhenIdle boolean on web, fail early when the page is idle instead of waiting the full timeout

title: Assertions
description: The full expect() API, including text/state checks, screenshots, accessibility, and auto-wait behavior.

sections.text: Assertions are made with the expect function from FlowContext . It takes a selector and returns a PromiseExpectation with chainable assertion methods. const { expect } = ctx; await expect({ testID: "welcome-banner" }).toBeVisible();

sections.heading: expect(selector)
sections.text: expect: (selector: ExtendedSelector) = PromiseExpectation; Returns a PromiseExpectation bound to the given selector. Any selector, including relative selectors, works here.

sections.heading: Core visibility, text, and state assertions
sections.text: Method Signature Description ----------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------- toBeVisible (opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert that the element exists and is visible toBeHidden (opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert that the element is missing or hidden toHaveText (expected: string, opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert an exact text match toContainText (expected: string, opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert a case-insensitive substring match toMatchText (pattern: RegExp, opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert a regular-expression text match toHaveValue (expected: string \ number, opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert an exact form value match toHaveAttribute (name: string, value?: string, opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert that an attribute exists or matches a value toBeEnabled (opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert that the element is enabled toBeDisabled (opts?: WaitOptions) = Promise Assert that the element is disabled await expect({ testID: "success-message" }).toBeVisible(); await expect({ text: "Welcome" }).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8000 }); await expect({ testID: "user-greeting" }).toHaveText("Hello, Alice"); await expect({ testID: "status" }).toContainText("saved"); await expect({ testID: "price" }).toMatchText(/^\$\d+\.\d{2}$/); await expect({ testID: "email" }).toHaveValue("demo@example.com"); await expect({ testID: "primary-button" }).toHaveAttribute("aria-busy", "false"); await expect({ testID: "submit" }).toBeEnabled(); Use toHaveText() for exact text, toContainText() for partial copy, and toMatchText() when you need more flexible matching.

sections.heading: Visual regression
sections.text: toMatchScreenshot( name: string, options?: { threshold?: number; maxDiffPixelRatio?: number; }, ): Promise Capture the current element and compare it against a named baseline image. When no baseline exists yet, spana writes the current screenshot as the baseline and the assertion passes. await expect({ testID: "avatar" }).toMatchScreenshot("profile-avatar"); await expect({ testID: "receipt" }).toMatchScreenshot("receipt", { threshold: 0.2, maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01, }); Create or refresh baselines with spana test --update-baselines . For suite-wide defaults, configure visualRegression in spana.config.ts .

sections.heading: Accessibility assertions
sections.text: Method Signature Description -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- toPassAccessibilityAudit (options?: { severity?: "critical" \ "serious" \ "moderate" \ "minor"; rules?: string[]; exclude?: Selector[] }) = Promise Run an axe-core audit of the current web page toHaveAccessibilityLabel (expected?: string) = Promise Assert that an element has an accessibility label, optionally with an exact value toBeFocusable () = Promise Assert that the element can receive focus toHaveRole (expected: string) = Promise Assert a semantic role such as button or link toHaveMinTouchTarget (size?: number) = Promise Assert a minimum touch target size, default 44 await expect("body").toPassAccessibilityAudit({ severity: "serious", rules: ["color-contrast", "button-name"], }); await expect({ testID: "login-button" }).toHaveAccessibilityLabel("Log in"); await expect({ testID: "login-button" }).toHaveRole("button"); await expect({ testID: "login-button" }).toBeFocusable(); await expect({ testID: "login-button" }).toHaveMinTouchTarget(48); toPassAccessibilityAudit() is web-only. The other accessibility assertions are element-level checks that work across supported platforms.

sections.heading: Soft assertions and retrying custom checks
sections.text: await expect.soft({ testID: "name" }).toHaveText("Ada"); await expect.soft({ testID: "email" }).toContainText("@example.test"); await expect .poll(() = app.evaluate ("window.pendingRequests"), { timeout: 3000, intervals: [100, 250], }) .toBe(0); await expect(async () = { await expect({ testID: "ready" }).toBeVisible({ timeout: 200 }); await expect({ testID: "queue" }).toHaveText("Empty", { timeout: 200 }); }).toPass({ timeout: 3000, intervals: [100, 250] }); Soft assertions still wait for their matchers, including negated selector assertions such as expect.soft(selector).not.toBeVisible() . If they fail, the flow continues and reports the collected failures at the end of the attempt. poll compares a callback's return value and supports negation (for example, expect.poll(fn).not.toBe(0) ). toPass retries a callback until it stops throwing or rejecting. Both stop waiting at the configured timeout, even if a callback is still running. Use idempotent callbacks, since they can run more than once. The default retry intervals are 50, 100, 250, and 500 ms; after the interval list is exhausted, its last interval repeats.

sections.heading: ARIA snapshots
sections.text: On the Playwright web engine, compare a locator's accessible roles, names, and hierarchy against Playwright's YAML snapshot output: await expect({ css: "nav" }).toMatchAriaSnapshot( - navigation "Menu": - link "Home" - link "Settings" ); await expect({ css: "nav" }).toMatchAriaSnapshot({ path: "snapshots/menu.aria.yml" }); The assertion compares exact normalized YAML, ignoring leading indentation and surrounding blank lines. File paths are relative to the flow file. Run spana test --update-baselines to write or refresh file-based baselines; inline snapshots are edited by hand.

sections.heading: Auto-wait behavior
sections.text: All assertions auto-wait. spana does not require manual sleep() calls. On web, when the DOM channel is connected, spana first waits inside the page with a MutationObserver , so most assertions resolve in a single round trip. Otherwise (native screens, relative selectors, systemUI selectors) it uses this loop: 1. Dump the element hierarchy from the platform driver. 2. Search the tree for the selector. 3. Check the assertion condition. 4. If the condition is not met, wait and retry using adaptive polling. 5. If timeout is exceeded, fail with a descriptive error including the selector and last known state. WaitOptions lets you tune assertion behavior: type WaitOptions = { timeout?: number; pollInterval?: number; initialPollInterval?: number; settleTimeout?: number; }; - timeout : maximum time to wait before failing - pollInterval : maximum poll interval once backoff ramps up - initialPollInterval : first poll interval before backoff grows - settleTimeout : how long the element must remain present before the lookup passes initialPollInterval and settleTimeout apply to element lookups ( toBeVisible() and actions). Text, value, attribute, and state assertions poll at a fixed pollInterval and ignore them. settleTimeout is useful for transitions and animations where the element briefly appears and disappears.

sections.heading: Timeout configuration
sections.text: Timeouts are resolved in this order (highest priority first): 1. opts.timeout passed directly to the assertion method 2. flow(..., { defaults: { waitTimeout } }) on the containing flow 3. defaults.waitTimeout in spana.config.ts 4. Built-in default: 5000 ms // Global default in config defaults: { waitTimeout: 8000 }, }); // Per-flow override for waits and polling "slow screen test", { defaults: { waitTimeout: 12000, pollInterval: 250, settleTimeout: 300, }, }, async ({ expect }) = { // Per-assertion override await expect({ testID: "result" }).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 }); }, ); FlowConfig.timeout is a separate overall flow timeout. It does not replace assertion wait settings.

title: Platform-Specific Tests
description: Writing platform-aware tests using the platform context value and FlowConfig.platforms.

sections.text: spana runs a single flow file against multiple platforms. There are two mechanisms for platform-specific behavior: branching inside a flow, and restricting a flow to specific platforms entirely.

sections.heading: Branching inside a flow
sections.text: The platform value in FlowContext is "web" "android" "ios" "electron" "electrobun" . Use it for conditional logic within a flow that is mostly shared across platforms. await app.tap({ testID: "share-button" }); if (platform === "ios") { // iOS share sheet uses a native action sheet await expect({ text: "Copy Link" }).toBeVisible(); await app.tap({ text: "Copy Link" }); } else if (platform === "android") { // Android uses the system share dialog await expect({ text: "Copy to clipboard" }).toBeVisible(); await app.tap({ text: "Copy to clipboard" }); } else { // Web uses a custom share modal await expect({ testID: "share-modal" }).toBeVisible(); await app.tap({ testID: "copy-link" }); } await expect({ testID: "share-confirmation" }).toBeVisible(); });

sections.heading: Restricting a flow to specific platforms
sections.text: Use FlowConfig.platforms to prevent a flow from running on platforms where it does not apply. "push notification permissions", { platforms: ["android", "ios"] }, async ({ app, expect }) = { await app.tap({ testID: "enable-notifications" }); await expect({ testID: "permission-granted" }).toBeVisible(); }, ); This flow is skipped on web (and any other platform not in the list), even when that platform is part of the same run. FlowConfig.when.platform is different: it only drops the flow when none of the run's platforms match. See Conditional execution.

sections.heading: CLI platform filtering
sections.text: Regardless of per-flow platforms config, you can also filter at the CLI: Run only on web spana test --platform web Run on android and ios only spana test --platform android,ios CLI filtering takes effect before per-flow filtering. A flow with platforms: ["android"] will not run if you pass --platform web , even if both are in your config.

sections.heading: Device emulation and OS events
sections.text: API Playwright web Android iOS ----------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------ setGeolocation({ latitude, longitude }) Yes; also grant location access Local emulator or supported Appium driver Simulator or supported Appium driver setSystemTime(date) Yes; changes browser wall time without pausing timers — — grantPermission(name) , denyPermission(name) Grant via Playwright, deny via Chromium; optional { origin } Runtime permission names such as android.permission.CAMERA Simulator privacy services such as location setOrientation("portrait" \ "landscape") Swaps the viewport dimensions UiAutomator2 or Appium WDA or Appium setBiometricEnrollment(enabled) — Enroll a test fingerprint in Android settings first Simulator simulateBiometric(options) — Emulator; { type: "fingerprint", fingerId: 1 } Simulator; { type: "faceId", match: false } or type: "touchId" sendPushNotification(payload) — — Simulator; pass an APNs payload with an aps object await app.setBiometricEnrollment(true); await app.simulateBiometric({ type: "faceId", match: true }); await app.sendPushNotification({ aps: { alert: "Order shipped" }, orderId: "123" }); Guard calls by platform and target type. Appium support depends on the provider and driver version. Device changes can persist in reused devices or browser contexts; restore state explicitly where needed. Android system notifications posted by the shell do not deliver FCM messages to an app, so Android push simulation is not exposed.

sections.heading: System UI on mobile
sections.text: Out-of-process OS UI (permission dialogs, share sheets, in-app browser tabs) is not part of the app's DOM. Mark those selectors with systemUI so spana goes straight to the native driver: await app.tap({ testID: "enable-notifications" }); await app.tap(systemUI({ text: "Allow" })); });

sections.heading: Platform-specific selectors
sections.text: Some elements have the same semantic purpose but different identifiers across platforms. Assign the selector based on platform: const menuSelector = platform === "ios" ? { accessibilityLabel: "Main menu" } : { testID: "menu-button" }; await app.tap(menuSelector); });

sections.heading: Skip web for native-only features
sections.text: "biometric authentication", { platforms: ["ios", "android"] }, async ({ app, expect }) = { await app.tap({ testID: "use-biometrics" }); await expect({ testID: "biometric-success" }).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 }); }, );

sections.heading: Deep link only on mobile
sections.text: if (platform !== "web") { await app.openLink("myapp://profile/settings"); } else { await app.tap({ testID: "settings-nav" }); } await expect({ testID: "settings-screen" }).toBeVisible(); });

sections.heading: WebAssembly (WASM), WebGL2 / WebGPU & Canvas Apps
sections.text: Spana has first-class support for DOM-based WASM frameworks (Leptos, Yew, Dioxus, Blazor, Kotlin/Wasm), WebGL2/WebGPU apps (Flutter Web CanvasKit/Skwasm, Bevy, Godot, Unity, egui, Slint, Rive), multi-threaded SharedArrayBuffer / Web Worker apps (SQLite-WASM, DuckDB-WASM, FFmpeg.wasm), and headless WASI/in-process .wasm modules.

sections.heading: Deterministic Headless WebGL2 / WebGPU
sections.text: Enable ANGLE SwiftShader (and optional WebGPU) in spana.config.ts so headless CI renders pixel-deterministically without a physical GPU: execution: { web: { engine: "cdp", gpu: "swiftshader", // "auto" "swiftshader" "hardware" "disabled" webgpu: true, contextIsolation: "hot-cache", // keeps V8/Wasm compile cache warm, wipes OPFS + IDB + storage }, }, });

sections.heading: Canvas Semantic Tree, Low-Level Input & WASM Assertions
sections.text: Canvas-rendered WASM apps can register logical UI nodes via registerWasmSemanticTree from spana-bridge/wasm (or window. SPANA WASM TREE ), making { testID } and { role, name } work identically on as on HTML DOM. Flutter Web apps can activate ARIA semantics with await app.enableFlutterSemantics() . await app.openLink("/"); await app.waitForWasmReady(); const iso = await app.checkCrossOriginIsolation(); // Verifies COOP/COEP headers for SharedArrayBuffer / pthreads await app.tap({ testID: "canvas-save" }); await app.mouse.wheel(0, 120, { x: 400, y: 300 }); await app.dragXY(100, 150, 320, 150, { steps: 10 }); await app.tapOffset({ css: " viewport-canvas" }, 24, 24); await app.clock.nextFrame(2); await app.waitForCanvasStable({ css: " viewport-canvas" }); await expect.noWasmTraps(); // main thread + attached Web Workers await expect.wasmMemoryBelow("128MiB"); await expect.minFps(30, { durationMs: 500 }); });

sections.heading: Headless WASI / In-Process .wasm Testing
sections.text: Use createWasmDriver or registerDriverAdapter(createWasmDriverAdapter({ modulePath: "./app.wasm", runtime: "in-process" "wasi" "wasmtime" })) to run Spana flows directly against compiled .wasm modules with zero browser overhead.

title: Gherkin / BDD
description: Write tests as .feature files with Given/When/Then step definitions.

sections.text: Spana supports Gherkin-style BDD tests alongside the standard flow API. Write human-readable .feature files, then implement step definitions in TypeScript.

sections.heading: Project structure
sections.text: flows/ login/ login.feature Gherkin scenarios steps/ login.steps.ts Step definitions dashboard.flow.ts Standard flow (both styles coexist) When the run includes .feature files, spana searches the whole flowDir and loads every .steps.ts file and every .ts file inside a steps/ directory. Step definitions are global, so any step file can serve any feature.

sections.heading: Writing a feature file
sections.text: title="flows/login/login.feature" @e2e @auth Feature: User login Background: Given I am on the login screen @smoke @web @android @ios Scenario: Successful login When I enter "user@example.com" in the email field And I enter "password123" in the password field And I tap the login button Then I should see the text "Welcome" @web @android Scenario Outline: Navigate to When I navigate to " " Then I should see the element " " Examples: page path selector dashboard /dash dash-title settings /settings settings-title

sections.heading: Tags as platform filters
sections.text: Tags like @web , @android , and @ios on a feature, scenario, or Examples block control which platforms the scenario runs on. @timeout:90000 sets the scenario's flow timeout in ms. Other tags (like @smoke , @e2e ) keep their @ prefix, so filter them with --tag @smoke . Scenarios do not launch the app automatically ( autoLaunch is false ). Launch or navigate in a Background step or a Before hook.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Background steps run before every scenario in the feature, similar to a beforeEach hook.

sections.heading: Scenario Outline
sections.text: Use Scenario Outline with an Examples table to run the same scenario with different data. Placeholders like are replaced with values from each row.

sections.heading: Writing step definitions
sections.text: Step definitions map Gherkin steps to TypeScript functions. Import them from spana-test/steps : title="flows/login/steps/login.steps.ts" Given("I am on the login screen", async ({ app }) = { await app.launch({ deepLink: "myapp://login" }); }); When("I enter {string} in the email field", async ({ app }, email) = { await app.tap({ testID: "email-input" }); await app.inputText(email as string); }); When("I enter {string} in the password field", async ({ app }, password) = { await app.tap({ testID: "password-input" }); await app.inputText(password as string); }); When("I tap the login button", async ({ app }) = { await app.tap({ testID: "login-button" }); }); Then("I should see the text {string}", async ({ expect }, text) = { await expect({ text: text as string }).toBeVisible(); }); Then("I should see the element {string}", async ({ expect }, testID) = { await expect({ testID: testID as string }).toBeVisible(); });

sections.heading: Step keywords
sections.text: Function Purpose -------- ----------------------------- Given Set up preconditions When Perform actions Then Assert outcomes And Continue the previous keyword But Negative continuation All five register steps the same way -- the keyword is for readability only. Matching ignores the keyword, so a step registered with Given also matches a When or And line with the same text. Registering the same pattern twice throws an error, and a step line that matches more than one definition fails as ambiguous.

sections.heading: Pattern matching
sections.text: Step patterns support two forms: Cucumber expressions with placeholders such as {string} , {int} , {float} , and {word} : Then("I should see the element {string} within {int}ms", async ({ expect }, testID, timeout) = { await expect({ testID: testID as string }).toBeVisible({ timeout: timeout as number }); }); Regular expressions for complex matching: When(/^I swipe (left right up down)$/, async ({ app }, direction) = { await app.swipe(direction as string); }); Captured groups are passed as additional arguments after the context. A step's data table is passed as one more argument ( string[][] ), and a doc string as a string .

sections.heading: Step context
sections.text: Every step function receives the same context available in standard flows: Property Description ---------- ---------------------------------------------------------- app Full PromiseApp API (tap, inputText, scroll, etc.) expect Assertion helper platform Current platform ( "web" , "android" , "ios" ) sessions Open extra named web sessions state Map shared by all steps of the scenario If you define a world, its state fields and methods are also on the context.

sections.heading: Hooks
sections.text: Run setup/teardown code before or after each scenario: // Runs before every scenario Before(async ({ app }) = { await app.launch(); }); // Runs after every scenario After(async ({ app }) = { await app.takeScreenshot("after-scenario"); });

sections.heading: Tag-filtered hooks
sections.text: Restrict hooks to scenarios with specific tags: // Only runs before scenarios tagged @auth Before("@auth", async ({ app }) = { await app.launch({ deepLink: "myapp://login" }); });

sections.heading: World (shared state)
sections.text: Use defineWorld to share state and helper methods across steps within a scenario: title="flows/login/steps/world.ts" // Fresh state for each scenario create: () = ({ currentUser: "", authToken: "", }), // Helper methods available in step context methods: (ctx) = ({ async loginAs(email: string, password: string) { await ctx.app.tap({ testID: "email-input" }); await ctx.app.inputText(email); await ctx.app.tap({ testID: "password-input" }); await ctx.app.inputText(password); await ctx.app.tap({ testID: "login-button" }); ctx.currentUser = email; }, }), }); World state is created fresh for each scenario. The state map is also available for arbitrary key-value storage across steps. Only one world is active: the last defineWorld() call that spana loads wins.

sections.heading: Running Gherkin tests
sections.text: Gherkin tests run with the same CLI as standard flows: Run all tests (flows + features) spana test Filter by tag spana test --tag @smoke Filter by name spana test --grep "login" Run only on specific platforms spana test --platform web,android

sections.heading: Mixing flows and features
sections.text: Both .flow.ts (or .test.ts ) and .feature files can live in the same flowDir . Spana discovers and runs both. Use whichever style fits the test -- Gherkin for behavior specs, flows for lower-level or exploratory tests.

title: Varar (Markdown specs)
description: Run Varar Markdown documents as tests, with Spana driving web, iOS, Android and desktop apps.

sections.text: Varar turns plain Markdown documents into tests. A value in a sentence is either an input (a stimulus ) or an expected output (a sensor ). If the app returns a different value, the test fails. There are no Given / When / Then keywords. Varar runs inside Vitest. Spana does not run .md files itself. Instead, your step functions call Spana's Agent API ( connect() from spana-test/agent ) to drive the app. :::note[Which one to pick] Use Varar when you want specs that read like normal documentation. Use Gherkin when you already have .feature files. Use plain flows for the fastest runs: only spana test gives you the shared browser pool, --changed-since filters, reports and platform tags. ::: A full working project is in examples/varar .

sections.heading: Install
