sections.text: title=".github/workflows/test.yml" jobs: e2e: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 - run: bun install - run: spana test \ --platform android \ --appium-url "https://${{ secrets.BS USER }}:${{ secrets.BS KEY }}@hub-cloud.browserstack.com/wd/hub" \ --caps caps.json \ --caps-json '{"bstack:options": {"buildName": "${{ github.run id }}"}}'

title: CI/CD Integration
description: Run spana tests in continuous integration pipelines with structured reporting and artifacts.

sections.text: spana is designed for CI from the ground up. It ships as a single npm package ( spana-test ), produces machine-readable output via JSON and JUnit reporters, and uses standard exit codes so your pipeline can react to results without parsing logs.

sections.heading: Exit codes
sections.text: Code Meaning ---- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 0 No flow failed. This includes runs where no flows matched, --changed-since filtered out every flow, or a platform was skipped because no device was found. 1 At least one flow failed, or the command could not start (invalid options, a config that fails to load, missing Appium URL).

sections.heading: Reporters for CI
sections.text: Use the --reporter flag to control output format. Multiple reporters can be combined with commas. Machine-readable results for CI dashboards spana test --reporter json,junit Human-readable HTML report for review spana test --reporter html Combined: console output + JUnit + HTML spana test --reporter console,junit,html - junit — writes a JUnit XML file to spana-output/junit-report.xml , understood by most CI systems. - json — prints one JSON event per line to stdout ( flowPass , flowFail , runComplete ), useful for piping to other tools. - html — writes an HTML report to spana-output/report.html with screenshots and step details. - allure — writes Allure result files for an Allure report. - github — writes a PR-ready Markdown summary ( spana-output/github-pr-summary.md ) and appends directly to $GITHUB STEP SUMMARY in GitHub Actions. The output directory is artifacts.outputDir (default ./spana-output ). Per-flow artifacts (screenshots, hierarchy.json , failure-bundle.json ) go in spana-output/ - / .

sections.heading: PR-Aware CI Filtering (--changed-since)
sections.text: Run only the flows affected by a pull request while staying fail-open . --changed-since diffs against git merge-base HEAD and runs the filters from spana.config.ts in order. --changed-since does nothing without a filters list in config: spana prints a warning and runs all flows. If git fails (for example, the base ref is missing in a shallow clone), spana also fails open and runs all flows. If one filter throws, that filter is skipped and keeps every flow it received (flows an earlier filter excluded stay excluded). If the filters exclude every flow, the run exits 0 . Built-in filters (all exported from spana-test ): - pathRuleFilter — deterministic, no LLM. Maps flow tags or file prefixes to watched source paths. Flows that no rule owns always run. - deterministicImpactFilter — deterministic, no LLM. Uses path mappings and the import graph; by default, unmapped changes run everything. - decisionFilter — asks a model judge ( createLogprobDecisionJudge or createOllamaDecisionJudge ) how likely each flow is affected, and skips flows below threshold (default 0.20 ). All three always keep changed flow files and flows with alwaysRunTags , and run everything when spana.config. or a lockfile changes or a runAllOnPaths prefix matches. decisionFilter also runs everything when the diff exceeds maxDiffBytes (default 60 kB) and keeps a flow when the judge errors. // spana.config.ts defineConfig, decisionFilter, createLogprobDecisionJudge, pathRuleFilter, } from "spana-test"; filters: [ pathRuleFilter({ rules: [{ matchFlow: { tag: "billing" }, watchPaths: ["src/billing/"] }], }), decisionFilter({ alwaysRunTags: ["smoke"], judge: createLogprobDecisionJudge({ provider: "openai", // works with vLLM, SGLang, llama-server, Typesafe AI, OpenRouter, or "ollama" baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", model: "typesafe-ai/jev", }), }), ], }); - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 required for merge-base diffing - name: Run affected E2E flows run: - npx spana test --parallel --workers 4 --reporter console,junit,github ${{ github.event name == 'pull request' && format('--changed-since origin/{0}', github.base ref) '' }} createLogprobDecisionJudge places the shared git diff prefix first in every prompt so vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp can reuse the KV cache across every flow in the PR. It requests a single token ( YES / NO ) with logprobs and turns the top logprobs into a probability. Spana also persists per-flow durations in spana-output/.spana/last-run.json . On later runs, multi-worker runs ( --parallel / --workers / --devices ) schedule the slowest flows first ( orderFlowsLongestFirst ), and --shard uses the durations to balance shards. Cache this file between CI runs to keep the benefit.

sections.heading: Using the reusable action
sections.text: The spana repository contains a composite GitHub Action ( .github/actions/spana-test ) that handles installation, test execution, and artifact upload. The examples below reference it as a local action, so copy it into your repository first: name: E2E Tests on: [push, pull request] jobs: e2e-web: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - run: npm ci - run: npm run dev & - run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 - name: Run E2E tests uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test with: platform: web reporters: console,junit,html e2e-android: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - run: npm ci - name: Set up Android emulator uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2 with: api-level: 33 script: echo "Emulator ready" - name: Run E2E tests uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test with: platform: android retries: 1 e2e-ios: runs-on: macos-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - run: npm ci - name: Boot iOS Simulator run: xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 15" xcrun simctl bootstatus "iPhone 15" -b - name: Run E2E tests uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test with: platform: ios Action inputs Input Default Description ------------------- -------------------- --------------------------------------------------------- platform web Platform to test (web, android, ios) reporters console,junit,html Comma-separated reporter names config — Path to spana.config.ts flow-path — Path to flow files or directory device — Target a specific device by ID retries — Number of retries for failed flows tags — Filter by tags grep — Filter by name pattern working-directory . Directory to run spana in version latest spana-test version to install upload-artifacts true Upload spana-output/ and allure-results/ as artifacts The action also sets a result output ( pass or fail ).

sections.heading: Manual workflow setup
sections.text: If you prefer full control over the workflow steps: name: E2E Tests (Web) on: [push, pull request] jobs: e2e-web: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Install spana run: npm install -g spana-test - name: Install Chromium run: npx playwright install chromium - name: Start app run: npm run dev & - name: Wait for app run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 - name: Run tests run: spana test --platform web --reporter console,junit,html - name: Upload JUnit results if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: junit-results path: spana-output/junit-report.xml - name: Upload HTML report if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: html-report path: spana-output/report.html - name: Upload per-flow artifacts (screenshots, hierarchy, failure bundles) if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: spana-output path: spana-output/

sections.heading: Android tests
sections.text: Android tests need the Android SDK. GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners include the SDK, but you need to boot an emulator. e2e-android: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - name: Install spana run: npm install -g spana-test - name: Set up Android emulator uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2 with: api-level: 33 script: adb wait-for-device spana test --platform android --reporter console,junit,html - name: Upload test artifacts if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: android-results path: spana-output/

sections.heading: iOS tests
sections.text: iOS tests require a macOS runner with Xcode installed. e2e-ios: runs-on: macos-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 24 - name: Install spana run: npm install -g spana-test - name: Boot iOS Simulator run: xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 15" xcrun simctl bootstatus "iPhone 15" -b - name: Install app and run tests run: spana test --platform ios --reporter console,junit,html - name: Upload test artifacts if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: ios-results path: spana-output/

sections.heading: GitLab CI
sections.text: e2e-web: image: node:20 stage: test script: - npm ci - npm install -g spana-test - npm run dev & - npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 - spana test --platform web --reporter console,junit,html artifacts: when: always paths: - spana-output/ reports: junit: spana-output/junit-report.xml GitLab natively parses JUnit XML when declared under artifacts.reports.junit , so test results appear directly in merge request widgets.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text: - Combine reporters. Use --reporter console,junit,html to get terminal output for logs, JUnit for CI dashboards, and HTML for manual review — all in one run. - Upload spana-output/ as artifacts. This directory contains JUnit XML, HTML reports, and per-flow screenshots, hierarchies, and failure bundles. Always upload with if: always() (GitHub Actions) or when: always (GitLab) so artifacts are available even when tests fail. - Headless web works out of the box. Web runs are headless by default ( execution.web.headless ). No xvfb or display server setup needed. Install a browser on the runner first ( npx playwright install chromium ). The playwright engine needs it; the cdp engine uses it when present and otherwise falls back to a system Chrome. - Pick a web engine. execution.web.engine accepts "playwright" (default), "cdp" , "lightpanda" , or "auto" . "auto" uses the direct CDP engine for Chromium unless wsEndpoint , channel , or artifacts.har needs Playwright. - Scale web workers. --workers runs n isolated browser contexts, spread over browser processes by execution.web.maxContextsPerBrowser . - Split across jobs. --shard / runs one slice of the flows per CI job. - Use tags to split pipelines. Run spana test --tag smoke on every push and spana test --tag regression on a nightly schedule to balance speed and coverage. - Pin spana version. Use npm install -g spana-test@ (for example spana-test@0.7.0 ) in CI to avoid unexpected breakage from new releases.

title: Debugging
description: Debug failing tests interactively with the built-in REPL.

sections.text: When a test fails, spana can drop you into an interactive REPL connected to the live device session. This lets you inspect the screen, try selectors, and experiment with actions before the session is torn down.

sections.heading: Enabling the debug REPL
sections.text: spana test --debug-on-failure When a flow fails, instead of moving to the next flow, spana pauses and opens a REPL: Entering debug REPL for failed flow "login flow" on android. Available bindings: app, expect, driver, platform, flowName, error, hierarchy(), selectors(), help() Use top-level await for async calls, for example: await app.tap({ text: "Login" }) spana:android

sections.heading: Available bindings
sections.text: Binding Type Description ------------- -------- ---------------------------------------------------- app object Full PromiseApp API -- tap, inputText, scroll, etc expect function Assertion helper, same as in flows driver object Raw driver service for low-level access platform string Current platform ( "web" , "android" , "ios" ) flowName string Name of the failed flow error Error The error that caused the failure hierarchy() async Returns the parsed UI element tree selectors() async Returns suggested selectors for visible elements help() function Print all available bindings

sections.heading: Example session
sections.text: spana:android error.message 'Timed out waiting for selector { testID: "welcome-text" }' spana:android await selectors() [ { suggestedSelector: { testID: 'login-button' }, elementType: 'Button', text: 'Sign In' }, { suggestedSelector: { text: 'Welcome' }, elementType: 'Text', text: 'Welcome' }, ... ] spana:android await app.tap({ text: "Sign In" }) undefined spana:android await expect({ testID: "welcome-text" }).toBeVisible() undefined spana:android .exit

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text: - Use await selectors() to discover what's on screen -- this is the fastest way to find the right selector - Use await hierarchy() for the full element tree with bounds, visibility, and nesting - All app methods use auto-wait, so await app.tap(...) will retry until the element appears - The REPL only activates once per test run (the first failure) to avoid blocking CI - The REPL requires an interactive terminal (TTY on both stdin and stdout) -- it's skipped automatically when there is none, as in most CI environments - Type .exit or press Ctrl+D to leave the REPL and continue the test run

sections.heading: Failure artifacts and --verbose
sections.text: Every failed flow writes artifacts to spana-output/ - / (by default artifacts.captureOnFailure is on): a screenshot, hierarchy.json , and failure-bundle.json with the failing selector and nearby alternatives. Web runs also capture console logs and JS errors ( artifacts.consoleLogs / artifacts.jsErrors , on by default). Pass --verbose to print the failure category, message, suggestion, diagnostic sections, and stack trace in the terminal: spana test --verbose

sections.heading: Visual Playback & Video Recording
sections.text: Enable visual playback or video recording in spana.config.ts so anyone can visually scrub through every step in report.html (Play/Pause, 0.5×/1×/2× speed, timeline scrubber, red click-ripple indicator, synchronized step list, and embedded ). Both are off by default: artifacts: { playback: true, // Interactive timeline player in report.html video: "retain-on-failure", // "off" (default) "on" "retain-on-failure" }, reporters: ["console", "html"], }); How video is captured depends on the target: - Web -- CDP screencast ( Page.startScreencast ). This needs the direct CDP engine ( execution.web.engine: "cdp" , or "auto" when it resolves to cdp ). The frames are muxed to .mp4 only when ffmpeg is on PATH . - Android -- adb shell screenrecord . - iOS Simulator -- xcrun simctl io recordVideo . Where no screencast is available (for example the playwright web engine), playback: true builds the timeline from step screenshots, so also set artifacts.captureSteps: true .

sections.heading: Common Pitfalls Spana Protects Against & How to Fix Your App
sections.text: Spana catches both test flakiness and real application bugs. When a test fails, fix the root cause rather than adding sleep() calls: Pitfall How Spana protects you automatically Recommended fix in your app or config --------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Hydration / loading overlay swallows clicks Single-RTT in-page actionability verifies the target is visible, enabled, unobstructed via deep elementFromPoint , and stable for 2 animation frames before tapping. Expose window. SPANA APP READY = true once your SPA finishes initial hydration/auth boot; Spana automatically waits for it before interacting. Stale async fetches clobber UI state Fast Direct CDP interactions can expose out-of-order fetch() responses when users switch tabs or type rapidly. Guard async UI updates with an AbortController or monotonic request sequence ID ( if (seq !== latestSeq) return ) in your app components. Missing or brittle selectors Failure bundles list the exact attempted selector plus nearby visible alternatives. Add stable data-testid / testID attributes to interactive elements instead of matching localized copy or fragile CSS paths. Cross-origin (Stripe, OAuth) With the direct CDP engine ( engine: "cdp" or "auto" ), Spana auto-attaches to out-of-process iframes ( Target.setAutoAttach ) and translates element coordinates into top-level viewport space. Ensure elements inside your own embedded frames expose data-testid or accessible labels. Flaky animations & layout shift 2-rAF stability check waits for moving buttons to settle before clicking. Enable execution.web.instantAnimations: true in spana.config.ts to collapse CSS transitions to 0.001 ms during E2E runs. Accessibility regressions await expect().toPassAccessibilityAudit() (and spana assert accessible in MCP) runs axe-core and reports WCAG rules, severity, and offending nodes. Fix missing aria-label , heading order, color contrast, and form associations directly in the component rather than disabling rules. Visual diff noise from timestamps/avatars toMatchScreenshot() (Rust-accelerated when the native library is available) supports dynamic region masks and a layout-tolerant compare mode. Pass { mask: [{ testID: "live-clock" }] } to toMatchScreenshot() , set visualRegression.mode: "layout-tolerant" in config, or freeze clock/seed data in your fixture. Slow repeated UI login & cross-test state leaks freshContextPerFlow: true isolates cookies/storage per flow while pre-warming the next context in the background. Use definePersona() + PersonaAuthCache or createApiFixture() to seed state via API instead of clicking through login in every test.

title: Recommended Fast TypeScript Toolchain
description: Opinionated guide to the fastest 2–3 tools in every TypeScript category — package managers, type-checkers, linters, formatters, bundlers, unit/component runners, and cross-platform E2E.

sections.text: Fast E2E tests are only one part of a fast developer loop. If install , type-checking, linting, bundling, or unit tests take minutes, your team still waits on every push. Below are the top 2–3 fastest TypeScript tools in every category , organized by use case and trade-offs. Every pick focuses on real wall-clock speed without sacrificing ergonomics. :::tip[Opinionated, not dogmatic] Newer native tools ( tsgo , tsrs , turbo-dom , bun lint , bun fmt ) are moving rapidly. Each table notes when to pick the fastest native option vs. when to stay with a battle-tested default. ::: ---

sections.heading: 1. Runtime & Package Manager
sections.text: Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs --------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Bun All-in-one TS apps, monorepos, CLI & test runners Native Zig runtime + package manager + bundler + test runner + linter/formatter. Direct .ts execution with near-instant installs ( bun install ). pnpm Strict Node.js monorepos & enterprise CI Content-addressable global store + hard links save disk & install time while keeping 100% Node.js runtime compatibility. Node.js 24+ (strip-types) Conservative enterprise environments Native TypeScript type-stripping built in; pair with pnpm or Corepack when Bun isn't allowed in production. ---

sections.heading: 2. Type-Checking
sections.text: Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- tsgo ( @typescript/native-preview ) Official TypeScript 7 speedups Microsoft's native Go port of tsc — typically 5–10× faster type-checking and lower memory across large monorepos. tsrs (Oxc ecosystem) Rust/WASM toolchains & ultra-low memory Rust port of the TypeScript compiler maintained in the Oxc ecosystem with WASM ( wasm32-wasip1 ) support. Rapidly evolving — test against your repo before replacing tsc as the merge gate. tsc --noEmit --incremental Codebases using TS language-service plugins Still the source of truth when you rely on compiler/language-service plugins (e.g. @effect/language-service ). Use --incremental + Turborepo caching to keep CI fast. ---

sections.heading: 3. Linting & Formatting
sections.text: Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- bun lint & bun fmt Zero-dependency Bun repos Built directly into Bun. bun lint covers 1,000+ ESLint / typescript-eslint / React / unicorn / a11y rules (including type-aware rules) and reads existing ESLint/Oxlint configs; bun fmt is a Prettier-compatible native formatter across TS, JSX, CSS, HTML, JSON, YAML, and Markdown ( 569 ms on 12k files). tidy (pair with oxlint or bun lint ) Maximum raw formatting speed with Prettier parity Single Rust binary by Luke Edwards — checks 12,000+ files in 280 ms ( 2× faster than bun fmt , 4–8× faster than oxfmt , 66–108× faster than Prettier), formats embedded HTML/Vue/Markdown/JS-template code, and fixes Prettier idempotency edge cases ( cargo binstall tidy or bun add tidyrs ). Oxlint & Oxfmt High-speed Node or Bun monorepos Rust-native linter (50–100× faster than ESLint) and formatter from VoidZero/Oxc — what Spana's own monorepo uses ( oxlint . checks 347 files in 40 ms, pure npm devDependency with zero extra binary install). Biome Single-binary lint + format with one config Mature Rust linter + formatter in a single biome.json file; great drop-in replacement for ESLint + Prettier in standard JS/TS repos. ---

sections.heading: 4. Bundlers & Library Builds
sections.text: Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Vite (Rolldown) & tsdown Web apps & npm TypeScript libraries Rust-backed Rollup-compatible bundling via Rolldown, keeping the full Vite plugin ecosystem with native build speeds. bun build CLIs, backend services & zero-config bundles Built into Bun; single-file executables and sub-100 ms bundles with zero extra devDependencies. Rsbuild / Rspack Large Webpack migrations Rust drop-in compatible with Webpack configs/loaders when migrating legacy enterprise apps without rewriting build plugins. ---

sections.heading: 5. Monorepo Task Runners
sections.text: Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs ------------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Turborepo Most TypeScript monorepos Minimal turbo.json setup, content-hashed local + remote caching, parallel task graph execution. Nx Large orgs needing affected graphs & generators Rich project-graph analysis, distributed CI task execution, and deep framework plugins. Bun Workspaces ( bun --filter ) Small-to-medium repos (< 10 packages) Zero extra tooling; fast workspace filtering built directly into Bun. ---

sections.heading: 6. Unit & Component Testing (Below E2E)
sections.text: Keep business logic and UI component tests fast at the base of the pyramid, and save real-browser E2E for critical user journeys. Tool Best for Why it's fast / trade-offs ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- bun test Pure TypeScript logic, API & driver unit tests Native Jest-compatible runner with instant startup (Spana runs 850+ tests in 30 s including live Chrome specs). Vitest + @miaskiewicz/turbo-dom (or happy-dom ) React / Vue / Svelte component tests Mature Vite-native runner paired with turbo-dom — a Rust html5ever -backed drop-in DOM environment with 99.94% html5lib conformance (vs happy-dom 37.35%, jsdom 97.03%) that runs Testing Library, user-event , Radix UI, and Headless UI unmodified. turbo-test Maximum-speed Vitest-compatible component suites Runs standard .test.ts(x) directly in a native V8 + Rust turbo-dom process, bypassing Node + jsdom bottlenecks entirely. :::note[Why not use turbo-dom for E2E?] @miaskiewicz/turbo-dom 's npm runtime intentionally has no CSS layout engine ( top / left are 0 , @media and :hover rules aren't evaluated). That makes it ideal for fast component tests, while real E2E tests belong in real browsers and WebViews. ::: ---

sections.heading: 7. E2E Testing (Web, Mobile & Desktop)
sections.text: Pick the E2E tool that matches your target matrix:

sections.heading: Cross-Platform (Web + iOS + Android + Electron + Electrobun)
sections.text: Tool Best for Strengths ------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Spana One TypeScript suite across Web, Capacitor/RN Mobile & Desktop Direct CDP on Chromium (1.5–1.7× faster than Playwright in strict fresh-context mode, up to 3.8× with hot-cache ), direct WDA/UiAutomator2 on mobile (no Appium), composable selectors ( byRole , within , inFrame ), WebAuthn passkeys, --processes dynamic work-stealing queue, --changed-since CI filters, and built-in spana mcp . e2e Agent-native web + mobile workflows Blends TypeScript steps with natural-language agent actions, built-in MCP server, and deterministic replay caching.

sections.heading: Web-Only
sections.text: Tool Best for Strengths ------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Spana Speed-first Chromium/WebKit/Firefox suites + MCP agent workflows Direct CDP engine, hot-cache isolation, per-persona passkey store, and CI PR impact filtering. Playwright Web-only teams wanting the largest ecosystem & Trace Viewer Battle-tested multi-language API, interactive trace.zip time-travel viewer, huge community.

sections.heading: React Native & Mobile-Focused
sections.text: Tool Best for Strengths --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Spana Shared Web + React Native / Capacitor suites in TypeScript Single .flow.ts codebase across Web + iOS + Android, direct WDA/UiAutomator2 without Appium, plus BrowserStack / Sauce Labs cloud support. Argent ( @swmansion/argent ) React Native-first teams & deep RN debugging Built by Software Mansion (core RN contributors). AI coding agents record flows into deterministic zero-AI YAML replays, with deep Hermes / React DevTools / Perfetto profiling, network/console capture, and physical USB device support. e2e / Maestro Mobile flows with minimal boilerplate e2e for agent-assisted TypeScript flows with replay cache; Maestro for simple YAML-first mobile scripts. ---

sections.heading: Example: The "Zero-Wait" 2026 Stack
sections.text: If you are starting a fresh TypeScript monorepo targeting Web + Mobile: - Runtime & installs: bun - Lint & format: bun lint + bun fmt (or oxlint + oxfmt ) - Type-check: tsgo (or tsc --incremental if using TS plugins) - Bundler: Vite (Rolldown) / tsdown - Unit & component tests: bun test + Vitest with @miaskiewicz/turbo-dom - E2E tests: Spana ( engine: "auto" , --workers 4 --processes 4 , --changed-since origin/main ), paired with Argent if you want deep Hermes/RN performance profiling alongside your E2E runs.

title: Privacy Policy
description: Privacy policy for the Spana documentation site (spana.antonwester.se).
